newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds drifted lower again on Monday, with investors still shunning the market as an expected snap French election added EMU worries to the established uncertainty over short-term U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
"It's very, very quiet again, there are just no flows from investors at all," one trader said.
"There is no big U.S. data to focus on this week, so I think all eyes are going to be on politics, both French and German."
President Jacques Chirac is expected to announce an early poll in France later this evening.
Implications of the decision for France's drive to qualify for monetary union were adding to unease over Germany's stuttering progress towards meeting the EMU deficit criterion, the trader said.

Dutch bonds tracked Bunds lower in the afternoon, but managed to squeeze some outperformance. At the longer end, the yield discount to Germany looked well supported and could even widen a little, a broker said.
A restricted issuance profile compared with Germany is seen favouring the local market. Just one issue is planned for the second quarter.
Analysts say this may virtually fulfil the Dutch state funding requirement for the year. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
